'''Curt Brunnée''' (24 May 1928 – 14 December 2023) was a German physicist known for his contributions to the field of [[mass spectrometry]] instrumentation.<ref name="pmid9149437">{{cite journal |vauthors=ten Noever de Brauw Michael C |title=A short story about the life of Curt Brunnée |journal=Rapid Commun Mass Spectrom |volume=11 |issue=6 |pages=708–13 |date=1997 |pmid=9149437 |doi=10.1002/(SICI)1097-0231(199704)11:6<708::AID-RCM905>3.0.CO;2-S }}</ref><ref name="encyclopedia">{{cite book |doi=10.1016/B978-0-08-100379-4.00063-0 |chapter=Curt Brunnée |title=The Encyclopedia of Mass Spectrometry |year=2015 |last1=Franz |first1=Andreas H. |pages=29–32 |isbn=978-0-08-100379-4 }}</ref> Brunnée was born on 24 May 1928.<ref name="pmid9149437"/> 

Brunnée married his long time laboratory assistant, Curta, in 1953.<ref name="pmid9149437"/> He died on 14 December 2023, at the age of 95.<ref>{{cite web |title=Dr. Curt Brunnée |url=https://trauer.weser-kurier.de/traueranzeige/curt-brunnee |website=WK Trauer |access-date=9 January 2024}}</ref>

==Career and research==
Brunnée grew up in [[Rostock]], his father was a dentist and his grandfather had a factory in [[Göttingen]] that produced optical instruments.<ref name="pmid9149437"/> During the war, his childhood home was destroyed by a bombing raid in 1942 and in 1944, the family narrowly escaped death as a bomb partially destroyed the cellar in which they were sheltering.<ref name="pmid9149437"/> Only after the war ended and schools resumed, could Brunnée finish his high school education and enter university.<ref name="pmid9149437"/> He entered the [[Universität Rostock]] in 1946, but fled in 1948 due to the increasingly repressive climate in eastern Germany, crossing the boundary between the [[Soviet occupation zone]] and the west illegally.<ref name="pmid9149437"/> He then enrolled at the [[Universität Marburg]], where he obtained his degree in physics in 1952 and completed his PhD in 1955 in the laboratory of [[Wilhelm Walcher]], who used a [[sector mass spectrometer]] for isotope separation.<ref name="encyclopedia"/> In 1956, he met Ludolf Jenckel (1912–1990) through his PhD advisor Walcher and joined the MAT division at [[Atlas Werke]] (a ship building company in [[Bremen]]) where Jenckel was building mass spectrometers.<ref name="encyclopedia"/>

The instrument the ATLAS-MAT division sold at the time (the {{Proper name|CH3}}) was not competitive with the instruments from the competition ([[Metrovick]] and [[Consolidated Engineering Corporation|CEC]]) and thus the {{Proper name|CH4}} instrument was developed, to which Brunnée contributed.<ref name="pmid9149437"/> In 1970 he became the head of the whole division with 280 employees. In 1988 he was promoted to worldwide research director of the [[Finnigan Instrument Corporation]] and retired in 1991.<ref name="encyclopedia"/> He received the [[International Mass Spectrometry Foundation#Awards|Thomson Medal]] from the [[International Mass Spectrometry Foundation]] (IMSF) in 1994 and the [[Curt Brunnée Award]] (IMSF) is named after him, which recognizes contributions to instrument development.<ref name="encyclopedia"/>
